decisions.reason: The anamnesis app was publicly launched as a new product line with its own page, sits close to the core software, and fits the firm's announced digital-practice direction, so commitment and sunk investment strongly favour keeping it.

The education institute builds on the firm's existing training content and customer relationships, and any weak results can be attributed to the temporary disruption of in-person courses during the pandemic, which supports persisting with it.
Remote screen-sharing support is cheap to maintain, is woven into the support process, and became more valuable during remote work, so there is little reason to drop it.

The analytics dashboard had its own page, reflects development effort, and is central to the announced direction of efficiently managed, connected practices, so management would persist even if uptake is slow.
The complete practice bundle packages the core offer, was given its own page, and serves new practices, so it is low-risk to keep and visibly tied to the firm's strategy.

The listing portal is distant from the core offer and was only mentioned on the website, so commitment is weaker, but it was cheap to run and its value as a community feature probably justifies keeping it for now.
